nodes.label: Raw Materials
nodes.subtitle: Ultra-pure inputs → wafers
nodes.description: Semiconductor manufacturing begins with extremely pure silicon that is shaped into wafers. These wafers act as the foundation on which billions of transistors are built.

nodes.label: Semiconductor Equipment
nodes.subtitle: Machines that make chips possible
nodes.description: Chipmaking depends on specialized tools that pattern, add, remove, and measure materials at nanometer scale. Tool precision sets the ceiling for how small and complex chips can get.

nodes.label: Wafer Fabrication (Foundries)
nodes.subtitle: Thousands of steps → transistors
nodes.description: Foundries manufacture chips designed by other companies. Advanced nodes like 3nm or 2nm require extremely complex manufacturing involving thousands of processing steps.

nodes.label: Chip Design
nodes.subtitle: Blueprints → architectures
nodes.description: Design teams turn workloads into architectures, then into layouts ready for fabrication. The design defines what the chip can do; manufacturing defines how efficiently it can be built.

nodes.label: Memory Manufacturing
nodes.subtitle: Hierarchy + bandwidth bottlenecks
nodes.description: Memory sits on a speed ladder: tiny and fast near the processor, larger and slower farther away. For AI, HBM is a key bottleneck because it must deliver enormous bandwidth close to the GPU.

nodes.label: Advanced Packaging & Testing
nodes.subtitle: Combine dies + memory at high speed
nodes.description: Modern AI chips are too complex to rely on a single piece of silicon. Advanced packaging connects multiple chips and memory components together with extremely high-speed connections.

nodes.label: Electronic Systems & Data Centers
nodes.subtitle: Chips become products
nodes.description: Semiconductors become real products: AI servers, smartphones, and vehicles. System-level constraints (power, cooling, networking) shape what the silicon needs to deliver.

nodes.label: Silicon
nodes.description: The base material for most chips. The trick is purity: contaminants at parts-per-billion can ruin device behavior.

nodes.label: Photoresist
nodes.description: Light-sensitive polymer that records patterns during lithography. Enables printing transistor features onto wafers.

nodes.label: Specialty Gases
nodes.description: High-purity gases used for etch and deposition. Gas quality directly affects yield and uniformity.

nodes.label: Lithography
nodes.description: Uses light to print transistor patterns onto silicon. Critical for making smaller and more powerful chips.

nodes.label: EUV
nodes.subtitle: Extreme ultraviolet lithography
nodes.description: EUV uses 13.5nm light to print the smallest features for leading-edge nodes. Tool availability and uptime gate capacity expansion.

nodes.label: Etching
nodes.description: Removes material to form microscopic structures. Precision determines line widths and device performance.

nodes.label: Deposition
nodes.description: Adds thin layers of materials onto the wafer. Layer thickness and uniformity are critical for transistor behavior.

nodes.label: Inspection & Metrology
nodes.description: Detects manufacturing defects and measures precision. Faster detection improves yield and ramp speed.

nodes.label: Process node
nodes.subtitle: e.g., 3nm / 2nm
nodes.description: A shorthand for a generation of manufacturing capability. Smaller nodes generally improve density and efficiency, but at higher complexity and cost.

nodes.label: Yield
nodes.description: The share of wafers that become good dies. Small yield changes can dominate unit cost and availability at ramp.

nodes.label: Capacity
nodes.description: How many wafers/chips can be produced over time. Constrained by tools, materials, labor, and time to qualify processes.

nodes.label: 3nm
nodes.description: A leading-edge process generation requiring EUV and tight process control. Often capacity- and yield-constrained in early ramps.

nodes.label: CPU
nodes.description: General-purpose processing optimized for sequential tasks and low latency.

nodes.label: GPU
nodes.description: Thousands of smaller processing units optimized for highly parallel workloads.

nodes.label: AI accelerator
nodes.description: Specialized chips designed for machine learning operations (matrix math at scale).

nodes.label: Networking chips
nodes.description: Move data between processors and systems. Often the hidden bottleneck in large-scale compute.

nodes.label: Memory hierarchy
nodes.description: Registers → cache → DRAM → storage. Closer is faster and smaller; farther is larger and cheaper.

nodes.label: HBM
nodes.subtitle: High Bandwidth Memory
nodes.description: Stacked memory placed close to AI GPUs to deliver extremely high bandwidth. Supply is a critical bottleneck for AI infrastructure.

nodes.label: CoWoS
nodes.description: A 2.5D packaging approach that integrates GPU dies with HBM stacks on an interposer for very high bandwidth and short links.

nodes.label: Chiplets
nodes.description: Splitting a system into multiple smaller dies connected inside one package. Improves yield and flexibility, but increases integration complexity.

nodes.label: 2.5D / 3D packaging
nodes.description: Techniques that connect dies with dense interconnects (interposers, TSVs) to improve performance per watt and bandwidth.

nodes.label: AI server
nodes.description: A compute system combining CPUs, GPUs, HBM, and networking. System constraints (power, cooling, networking) often become the limiting factor.

nodes.label: Data center
nodes.description: Large-scale facility that powers and cools compute. Capex cycles and power availability shape semiconductor demand.

nodes.label: ASML
nodes.description: EUV lithography tool supplier. EUV delivery schedules and uptime can gate leading-edge capacity.

nodes.label: Applied Materials
nodes.description: Broad tool portfolio across deposition, etch, and materials engineering. Key enabler of advanced process integration.

nodes.label: Lam Research
nodes.description: Etch and deposition specialist. Tool performance influences critical dimensions and yield.

nodes.label: KLA
nodes.description: Process control leader. Faster defect detection improves yield learning curves.

nodes.label: TSMC
nodes.description: Leading-edge foundry. Advanced nodes and packaging capacity are key constraints for AI chips.

nodes.label: Samsung Foundry
nodes.description: Leading-edge foundry competitor. EUV tool availability and process maturity affect capacity.

nodes.label: GlobalFoundries
nodes.description: Mature-node foundry focused on specialty processes. Often critical for power, RF, and automotive supply chains.

nodes.label: NVIDIA
nodes.description: AI GPU designer. Depends on foundry capacity, advanced packaging, and HBM supply.

nodes.label: AMD
nodes.description: CPU/GPU designer. Uses chiplets extensively and depends on foundry + packaging ecosystems.

nodes.label: Qualcomm
nodes.description: Mobile SoC designer. Depends on foundries and mature/leading nodes for smartphones.

nodes.label: Broadcom
nodes.description: Networking silicon supplier. Often a key link between compute and system-level throughput.

nodes.label: Apple
nodes.description: Designs custom SoCs for consumer devices. Leading-edge node access can be a competitive differentiator.

nodes.label: SK Hynix
nodes.description: HBM supplier. HBM output and quality often gate AI GPU shipments.

nodes.label: Samsung Memory
nodes.description: Major DRAM/NAND producer and HBM competitor. Memory cycles impact supply availability.

nodes.label: Micron
nodes.description: US memory manufacturer. Expanding HBM capabilities to serve AI demand.

nodes.label: TSMC Advanced Packaging
nodes.description: CoWoS and other advanced packaging capacity provider. A critical integration bottleneck for AI accelerators.

nodes.label: ASE Technology
nodes.description: OSAT provider supporting packaging and testing. Complements foundry capacity with assembly throughput.

nodes.label: Amkor
nodes.description: OSAT provider for advanced packaging. Helps expand packaging capacity beyond foundry captive lines.
